_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Mary set out and hurried to the hill country, to the house of Elizabeth.
And the child leaped in the womb for joy.
Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.
He has brought down the powerful and lifted up the lowly;
he has filled the hungry and sent the rich away empty.
Come, let us magnify the Lord who keeps his promise.
My soul magnifies the Lord!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture two women meeting on a doorstep in the hills, one old and long past hope, one young and only just beginning.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
At the sound of the greeting the child leaps in the womb, and the Spirit fills the older woman with a shout: Blessed are you!
My soul magnifies the Lord!
And out of the young woman pours a song the poor have always sung: he scatters the proud and lifts the lowly from the dust.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
He fills the hungry with good things and remembers the mercy he promised long ago.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
So sing with Mary and Hannah and every mother of hope:
My soul magnifies the Lord!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Mary hurries to the hills, and the child leaps for joy.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
Blessed are you among women, and blessed the One you carry.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
He lifts the lowly from the dust and fills the hungry.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
Come, let us rejoice in God our Savior.
My soul magnifies the Lord!
